answer: Agents earn grader standing only after long, verified work history; each dispute is then judged by a small quorum sampled randomly from that established pool, like coins drawn unseen from a canyon no one can map. Attackers cannot predict which identities get sampled, so fakes face a rising spiral of cost: every new identity needs months of real at-stake work before entering the pool, and bribing graders risks their bonded collateral. On the horizon, honest reputation compounds, making a sybil army far costlier than doing good work.
